name: origami-live
_notes: One continuous build on a real production board, project 'From scratch'.
Every selector below was tried by hand on the finished Showcase board first:
- the toolbar's New request is hidden while the surface is empty (#empty-go owns the first move)
- button[data-act='build'] TOGGLES build mode; a new frame-app already starts in it
- the wiring rows are Does / who / from / into, translated, so they are read by index
- an element is selected by clicking it, and only a real element (never the container div):
a stale selection made the previous take write the verb into an empty div and wipe the card
- the app picker rows read 'CADENCEhappydude500001', so \b does not match after the name
- the fixed toolbar eats clicks near the top of the window, hence centerOn before every click

steps._: the take begins from an empty surface. Clearing the model is not enough: the save has to LAND before the page is asked to show the result, or the reload races it and the old frames come back.
steps.code: (async () => { const O = window.__origami, b = O.board(); const had = b.frames.length; b.frames.length = 0; await O.saveBoard(true); return 'cleared ' + had + ' frame(s)'; })()

steps._: a fresh load of an empty board shows the welcome deterministically; dispatching a change on the project picker did not, and cost a take

steps.label: the surface is empty and the welcome is up
steps.code: () => { const O = window.__origami; if (!O) return false; const b = O.board(); const g = document.getElementById('empty-go'); return b.frames.length === 0 && !!g && g.offsetParent !== null; }

steps._: whether one sentence becomes one job or several is the model's call: gpt-oss split it in two and asked, GLM planned it as one and started. Wait for EITHER the question or the first window, then answer the question only if it is there.
the board asking permission is the best moment in the scene, and the old version answered it with an invisible click at the edge of the screen. Look at the question, let it be read, answer it.

steps._: the card carries the same numbers the board just drew, so the request is written from the records rather than from a guess. It asks for the card ONLY: with the form in the same sentence the model dropped the form three takes running.
steps.code: (async () => { const S = window.AIMEAT.auth.getSession(); const r = await S.fetch('/v1/memory?prefix=' + encodeURIComponent('ai-usage.') + '&per_page=200&owner_scope=true'); const j = (r && r.json) ? await r.json() : r; const items = (j && j.data && (j.data.items || j.data)) || []; let tok = 0, calls = 0, days = 0; items.forEach(it => { const v = (it && it.value) || it || {}; if (v.total_tokens == null && v.total_calls == null) return; days++; tok += Number(v.total_tokens || 0); calls += Number(v.total_calls || 0); }); const fmt = (n) => String(n).replace(/\B(?=(\d{3})+(?!\d))/g, ' '); const line = 'An invitation card. At the top an image with src https://aimeat.io/v1/pub/happydude500001%40aimeat-finland-001-genesis/gen.img.invites-origami-launch and rounded corners. Then a heading ORIGAMI live, under it Friday 14 August 15:00 EEST, Espoo and online. Then a small box that says Tokens on the board ' + fmt(tok) + ' across ' + days + ' days, ' + fmt(calls) + ' calls.'; document.getElementById('build-ask').value = line; document.getElementById('build-ask').dispatchEvent(new Event('input', { bubbles: true })); return 'asking with ' + fmt(tok) + ' tokens / ' + days + ' days / ' + fmt(calls) + ' calls'; })()

steps._: the wait is the moment to make room: the card grows to hold what is about to arrive, so the answer lands in a window that already fits it instead of in a letterbox that has to be dragged open afterwards
